current_answer: GitHub lists USD 10,000 in Enterprise-platform credits for a startup affiliated with a GitHub for Startups partner and funded from outside through Series B or earlier. The programme does not fit a bootstrapped team without those gates. Credits are applied to the submitted Enterprise account for up to 12 months; a valid payment method is required, and active products move to standard paid billing when the credit ends.

catalogue_card.text: GitHub lists USD 10,000 in Enterprise-platform credits for eligible startups for up to 12 months. The team needs outside funding through Series B or earlier, a GitHub for Startups partner, and a clean Enterprise and prior-benefit history. The credit ends on use or expiry; active products then move to standard paid billing. Country coverage, the full eligible-usage list, and post-credit prices are not published.

summary: GitHub lists USD 10,000 in credits for up to 12 months on an eligible startup's Enterprise account.
The published gates are a GitHub for Startups partner, outside funding through Series B or earlier, no Enterprise plan in the last six months, and no previous GitHub credits or Enterprise licences.
The credits cover Enterprise licence costs and eligible add-ons, including Copilot, Advanced Security, and other metered offerings.
A valid payment method is required. Credits end when consumed or after 12 months, and active products then move to standard paid billing.
GitHub does not support Enterprises with data residency in this programme. Country coverage, a complete eligible-usage list, post-credit prices, and an approval decision time are not published.
uncertainty: GitHub does not publish country coverage, a fixed list of every eligible add-on or metered service, or the standard price after credits end on the reviewed page.
GitHub states an onboarding email arrives within 24 hours after approval; it does not publish an approval decision time.
